sources.note: 'Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.' -- no OPD, survey or grammar ms for utu.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. (Utu = C23)
sources.note: Introduction sec. 6 (pp. viii-ix): 'The transcription is semi-phonemic', Utu fluctuating sounds listed; the words stress/accent/tone occur nowhere in the volume; C23 Utu forms carry vowel length but no stress marks (visual check of printed p. 2). Sec. 2: Silopi-Utu share >80% vocabulary.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl 1885/130077).
sources.note: Same survey-wide sentence, pp. 13-14: stress marking omitted because the stress patterning has not been well established. Nothing Utu-specific.

sources.note: Lists only Rosetta Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org (= Z'graggen 1980), Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List; no language description.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Classification and population (C23 Utu 583), sample cognate rows; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975b. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41.
sources.note: Village gazetteer (Asikan, Gilolo, Guteb, Malolo, Silaul, Utu); no phonology.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (DOI 10.15144/PL-C19)
sources.note: Survey-wide only, sec. 1.3.3 p. 6: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Utu (= language 10 'Ut') gets villages (2.21.12.17), segmental Mabuso-Stock typology (2.21.16: no voiced/voiceless stop contrast in Utu etc.), and Illustration 29 'Verb Structure in Utu' (pp. 154-155) with no stress marks; nothing on Utu stress.

sources.note: Nothing: TNG data = Z'graggen 1980 only; Newguineaworld pages are empty stubs; Wikipedia stub; Glottolog has no grammar/sketch/phonology entry.

sources.citation: Kasprus, Aloys. 1942-45. The languages of the Mugil District, NE-New Guinea. Anthropos 37-40: 711-778 (open scan + scanned at HU Berlin digi-hub, DE-11-001871413).
sources.note: p. 727: 'although the Utu language is closely allied to the Garus dialects it is not treated of in this paper as the material concerning this speech was left in New Guinea and lost.' The article's 'Notes on the Sound Attributes: 1. Stress' therefore do not cover Utu.
